body:
Google claims that AI Overviews generate advertising revenue equal to traditional search results. What this means for your marketing strategy

What are AI Overviews and how do they work?

AI Overviews represent a new functionality introduced by Google, which uses artificial intelligence to quickly synthesize relevant information about a query directly at the top of the results page. Instead of offering users just a list of links, Google generates a concise summary, based on credible sources, that answers the question without requiring the user to access an external website.

Google's claim: equal advertising revenue

During a recent conference, Google representatives stated that these AI-based overviews generate advertising revenue comparable to those from traditional search results. Specifically, Google maintains that displaying ads in the context of AI Overviews does not negatively affect the search engine's economic performance, and may even contribute to increased user engagement through a more efficient experience.

Global expansion of advertising in AI Overviews

Google has already begun the global expansion of the AI Overview feature in multiple languages and regions, simultaneously integrating sponsored ads directly within these sections. This transition marks a major shift in how digital advertising works on the Google platform, because ads no longer appear exclusively in traditional sections (such as Search Ads or Shopping), but are also inserted within automated responses generated by AI.

Impact on user behavior

With the introduction of AI Overviews, user behavior in Google Search changes considerably. Users interact faster with content, spend less time browsing through the list of links and tend to search for direct, concise and personalized answers. This behavior affects both organic impressions and CTR (Click-Through Rate) for certain types of classic content.

What does this mean for your digital marketing strategy?

The change brought by AI Overviews requires marketing agencies and brands to rethink their priorities. Here are some essential directions:

1. Adapting content for AI

Google's algorithms use content available on web pages to build AI Overviews. Thus, it is vital that your website pages include clear, concise and structured answers to specific questions. Using FAQ, list and bullet point formats can significantly increase the chance that your information will be selected in overviews.

2. Optimization for complex and conversational queries

Google has mentioned that AI Overviews are triggered especially by longer, conversational and more complex queries. Thus, it is important that your content strategy targets long-tail keywords and detailed questions (such as "how to", "what is the best way to", "why does X happen").

3. Redefining traditional SEO

SEO no longer means just ranking in the top links. In the AI Overviews era, it is essential that information is correct, complete and meets E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness) quality requirements. Brands that offer well-structured educational content will have better chances of appearing in AI summaries.

4. Increasing investment in integrated advertising

To remain competitive, many marketing specialists will be forced to allocate budgets for ads integrated in AI Overviews. These ads can appear in a highly relevant informational context, increasing conversion rate if they are correctly targeted and well optimized.

5. Performance monitoring and new formats

Being a technology in full evolution, it is essential to constantly monitor the performance of ads displayed in AI Overviews and analyze the differences compared to traditional results.

6. Comparison: Traditional search vs. AI Overview

Feature Traditional results AI Overviews
Format List of links Direct answer with embedded sources
Interaction User clicks to find out more User immediately receives the answer
Ad placement Ads above or below results Ads inserted directly in responses
User behavior More extensive exploration Rapid information consumption

7. Real scenario example

Imagine you own an online store that sells natural supplements. A search like "What are the best supplements for immunity in 2025?" can trigger an AI Overview that takes content from one of your well-optimized articles. If you include an FAQ section, clear structure and credible sources on that page, Google's AI could use exactly that text. Additionally, if you run Google Ads, your product can appear as an ad directly in that Overview.

8. The role of advertising in AI Overviews

Ads displayed in AI Overviews are much better contextualized. For example, if the user searches for "best laptops for video editing in 2025", relevant ads may include:

  • Direct links to tested and recommended products
  • Temporary offers with attractive titles
  • Comparisons between models supported by informative content

9. Optimizing Google Ads campaigns for AI

It's not enough to have an ad. It must:

  • Contain conversational keywords
  • Be relevant to user intent
  • Be supported by an informative and clear landing page

10. Measuring results and A/B Testing

Use Google Ads, Search Console and Analytics to compare:

  • Performance of pages displayed in AI Overviews vs traditional ones
  • CTR of ads in AI vs normal Search
  • Conversions generated by format

Apply A/B testing on headlines, descriptions and offers to better understand what works in AI. Using Google Ads and Google Search Console remains critical to understanding how these changes affect traffic and conversions.

Integrating artificial intelligence into your own campaigns

It's not just Google using AI. Brands need to follow this example, integrating AI into marketing strategy: content writing automation, predictive analysis for PPC campaigns, intelligent chatbots for customer service or offer personalization based on user behavior.

Risks and challenges for marketers

In addition to opportunities, introducing AI Overviews also brings challenges:

  • Organic traffic losses for certain types of content, because users no longer access source pages.
  • Increased competition for display in overviews and associated advertising.
  • Difficulties in direct performance measurement (not all interactions from overviews are transparent in Google reports).

Google's expansion of AI Overviews and advertising integration in these formats represents a major strategic shift in the digital marketing industry. Agencies and brands must quickly adapt their content, SEO and PPC strategies to remain relevant in an increasingly automated ecosystem. Artificial intelligence is no longer an option, but a necessity in any competitive marketing strategy.
